method: Compose normalized Mitchell B=C=1/3 taps with overlapping 4x4 half-res Bayer averaging. Combine weights addressing the same sensor site before squaring. RGGB red/blue each use 4 sites, green uses 8. Average interior output energy on each axis. Green is the sum of two disjoint parity lattices with half weight each.
checks: Every composed axis preserves DC to 1e-10
limitations: Independent, spatially stationary sensor noise; not correlated electronic noise.
Excludes border pixels; does not describe lens warps, white balance, camera-to-working-space transforms or nonlinear Oklab propagation.
Double precision analytical weights, not exact Rust f32 execution.
Not a production calibration or a color-parity pass.
conclusion: Overlapping demosaic covariance changes the red/blue resize-only estimate by about 7.7%, while green has half their sensor-relative variance. Current chroma NLM uses the red/blue average, so the green factor alone cannot repair the demonstrated chroma mismatch. A single area ratio is not a channel-correct propagation model.
